item.title: Rust Smart Pointers Complete Guide: Box, Rc, and RefCell Explained with Code Examples
item.description: Master Rust smart pointers: Box, Rc, RefCell, and the powerful Rc<RefCell<T>> combo. Learn heap allocation, reference counting, and interior mutability through vivid analogies. Beginner to intermediate level.

item.title: 200K Context Window——AI's "Memory Palace" Management
item.description: Deep dive into Claude Code's context management mechanism: 200K tokens isn't "unlimited memory," how it auto-compacts, precisely prunes, and budget allocates. Unveiling how AI manages massive code information within a limited context window.

item.title: Deep Dive into Rust Collection Memory Layout: Vec's Stability Guarantees vs HashMap's Pitfalls
item.description: Memory layout differences between Vec, String, and HashMap, proper patterns for unsafe self-referential structures, and how Miri detects cross-collection address invalidation

item.title: Go Memory Allocator: A Warehouse Manager's Tale
item.description: From 64MB warehouses to 8KB shelves, discover how Go's three-level cache architecture makes memory allocation blazing fast. Deep dive into arena, span, and size class design philosophy.

item.title: The Secret to 10x Rust Performance: Stop Cloning, Start Borrowing
item.description: Why is your Rust code running like a snail? You might be using clone() too much. This article explains how Rust's borrowing system can transform your code from sluggish to blazing fast.

item.title: Cut 40% Memory with Rust Sidecar—No Rewrites Required
item.description: Rust Sidecar pattern guide: Offload CPU-intensive tasks to Rust without rewriting your system. Real data: memory reduced from 1.9GB to 1.28GB, GC pauses from 42ms to 18ms. Includes complete code examples.

item.title: Rust Smart Pointers Explained: A Practical Guide to Box, Rc, and RefCell
item.description: Learn Rust smart pointers through vivid analogies and practical examples. Master Box, Rc, and RefCell to understand Rust's memory management system effortlessly
